summary: A personal essay reflecting on how local media shaped the municipal elections held on October 9, 2023 in the author's town. It describes the roles of The Daily Beacon, Voice of the Valley and MetroMatters in framing issues and candidates, and the challenge of sorting sensational content from substantive reporting. The author concludes that local media became a critical actor in the election, shaping the outcomes it observed.
one_line: A personal essay arguing that local newspaper, radio and online media shaped public opinion and outcomes in the town's October 9, 2023 municipal elections.
key_facts: The municipal elections in the author's town took place on October 9, 2023.
The three main local media channels were the newspaper 'The Daily Beacon', the radio station 'Voice of the Valley', and the online news portal 'MetroMatters'.
'The Daily Beacon' is described as being as trusted among locals as the town hall clock and provided comprehensive coverage with candidate profiles and policy analysis.
'Voice of the Valley' hosted talk shows where callers like Mrs. Elsie Turner of the Wickfield district raised concerns about the disappearance of local markets.
Young activist Marcus Delaney used 'Voice of the Valley' talk shows to campaign for greener public spaces.
'MetroMatters' offered live interviews via streaming platforms, real-time updates on candidate whereabouts, and electoral race highlights.
Sarah Johnson, a mayoral contender, surged in popularity after 'The Daily Beacon' ran a feature on her community outreach initiative 'Parks for Progress'.
Incumbent mayor Paul Thompson was hurt by an expose in 'The Daily Beacon' scrutinizing the city's faltering waste management system.
The campaign issues were repairing infrastructure, supporting local businesses and improving schools, but the author argues the media supplied the frames for discussing them.

The author says citizen journalists on 'MetroMatters' were democratizing but sometimes conflated personal bias with public interest journalism, while trained journalists provided scaffolding for informed voting.
On the eve of the election, 'The Daily Beacon' published profiles of regular townsfolk alongside the candidates; on election day coverage simmered in the background.
The author concludes that local media had become a critical actor in the election, shaping the very outcomes it observed.
